en: <Color:255,200,200,255>Hmm, so not everythin' goes accordin' to some master plan of yers, huh, Akiyama-san?<Color:Default>
Of course not. If I could do that, then I'd be like the Buddha keeping the Monkey King trapped in the palm of his hand.
<Color:255,200,200,255>It's amazin' you can make a reference like that off the top a' yer head!<Color:Default>
That's going too far. Even I can't make other people do what I want them to.
<Color:255,200,200,255>For real? What if you're sayin' that just to throw me off guard?<Color:Default>
Well, actually... Haha, you got me.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Hey, that's a nasty thing to joke about! Now I feel like whatever I say, I'm playin' right into yer hand.<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>All righty, I'm gonna do whatever I can to not get pulled off course by you! I won't listen to anythin' ya gotta say!<Color:Default>
Well, that puts a bit of a damper on things.
You're reading into it too much. I swear I have no such intentions.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Really? Then I'm just overthinkin' things? That kinda feels like a shame.<Color:Default>
Why? You said you didn't like other people getting their way with you. You should be happy.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Well, I...<Color:Default>
Wait, are you saying you might want me to have even more of a sway over you?
<Color:255,200,200,255>No, I don't! You're a jerk, Akiyama-san!<Color:Default>
Yikes, I guess you're in denial...
You like it, don't you?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Maybe! How could ya tell?<Color:Default>
People who usually have self-confidence get bothered when things don't go their way.
If they can acknowledge that the other person has the upper hand, it can lead to respect. They might even learn to like them.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Wow, I see! I guess if I got played to that degree, I might not be that mad!<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Akiyama-san, can I ask ya somethin' real quick?<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Do ya frequent any other clubs?<Color:Default>
Yeah. I'm not exactly from here, so when I'm in Tokyo, I go drinking at clubs out there too.
<Color:255,200,200,255>That makes sense...<Color:Default>
No. Lately I've only been coming here.
<Color:255,200,200,255>That's good to hear!<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Okay, mind if I ask ya one other thing?<Color:Default>
Whatever you want to know.
Okay, but just one more.
<Color:255,200,200,255>So, uh, Akiyama-san... Do you, uh, have a girlfriend?<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Ah, okay. I kinda figured. You're a pretty attractive guy, Akiyama-san.<Color:Default>
But it shouldn't matter that I do, right? That doesn't change anything between us.
<Color:255,200,200,255>But I don't want things to stay the same...<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>Uh, I mean, who me!? I didn't say nothin'!<Color:Default>
I heard you. Pretty clearly actually. About things not staying the same?
<Color:255,200,200,255>God, you're such a meanie, Akiyama-san! I said I didn't say nothin'!<Color:Default>
I didn't hear anything. Did you say something?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Liar! That's what ya'd say if ya <Italic>did</Italic> hear!<Color:Default>
I mean it. Why don't you try saying it again?
<Color:255,200,200,255>No, ya dummy! I'm not sayin' a thing! Yer bein' such a meanie!<Color:Default>
I don't. And at my age, admitting I'm single isn't something I say proudly.
<Color:255,200,200,255>Oh, okay! So, then whaddya think of me?<Color:Default>
What!? Do I have to answer?
<Color:255,200,200,255>Yeah!<Color:Default>
Oh, geez...
I said just one more question.
<Color:255,200,200,255>What? C'mon, this one only!<Color:Default>
Nope. Sorry. You should have asked that first.
<Color:255,200,200,255>You're terrible, Akiyama-san! It took a lotta guts for me to ask ya that!<Color:Default>
That's a secret. And guys who have secrets are more attractive.
<Color:255,200,200,255>What're ya talkin' about? You just said ya'd tell me whatever I wanted to know!<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>So, c'mon! Out with it!<Color:Default>
<Color:255,200,200,255>What're ya talkin' about? C'mon, whaddya think of me?<Color:Default>
Nope, I said just one more question.
<Color:255,200,200,255>I... But ya haven't answered anythin'! Ya can't pull that!<Color:Default>
I never promised I'd answer anything.
<Color:255,200,200,255>You're a jerk, Akiyama-san! And after I got my courage up to ask ya in the first place.<Color:Default>
Hey, is it just me, or are there a lot of foreigners here in Osaka?
It's not just you. Apparently, Osaka has the most foreigners anywhere in Japan.
Well, I'll be. I never had that impression before coming here, so I'm pretty surprised.
I've never really thought about it myself, but now that ya mention it, I do get a lotta foreign customers. Some of the girls on staff are from abroad too.
Really? It can't be the most in all Japan. I figured there'd be more in Roppongi or something.
How am I s'posed to know? I'm just sayin' that's what I heard.
Well, either way, there are clearly enough that would make the rumor appear true.
Osakans are outgoin' folks who'll make friends with anyone, so maybe it's easy for foreigners to settle down here?
I see. That's pretty different. People in Tokyo don't care that much for strangers and make outsiders feel unwelcome.
People from Tokyo may as well be foreigners, as far as I'm concerned.
For starters, I usually don't understand what they're sayin' anyways.
Well, then. Does that mean you don't really understand what I'm saying?
Hmm. I get maybe like half of it?
We Osakans listen just enough to latch onto the interestin' bits of what you're sayin'! Forget the rest.
But I'm the kind of guy who goes out of his way to explain things, so I'm a bit shocked.
Sure you do! They still speak Japanese.
Nuh-uh. They get caught up on the meanin' of words and get all argumentative. I don't like listenin' to that sorta thing.
How should they speak, then?
They oughta speak in more plain terms, and just keep the words comin', like this.
Well, at least the nuance comes across.
That's hard on Japanese people. We don't all speak good English, so how are we supposed to communicate?
You don't gotta worry about that. Ya just gotta say, "How ya doin'?" and then leave the rest to hand signals and body language.
You just call out to people like that? That takes no small amount of courage.
It's just the way it is. When Tokyo folk see foreigners in trouble, they pretend not to see 'em, right? Here in Osaka, we try to be more helpful.
I see. I could probably stand to learn from that spirit of openness.
Can they understand you?
They understand well enough.
Well enough, huh? Right.
Whatever you're sayin', they can mostly get the meanin' from yer attitude. Just smile after you're done.
Either way, when I'm talkin' to someone like that, I look at their face and try to guess where they're from.
That's pretty slow on the uptake! Most people would realize right away!
How can ya really know? If someone looks Indian to me and they say they like curry, I'll ask 'em if they're Indian and they'll say, "No, I'm Brazilian."
And all the while I thought the person was Japanese. Brazilian, and likes curry! What're the chances?
Haha! That's a double surprise.
I really like the cityscape of Sotenbori. There's something nice about having a river run right through the middle of the city.
Really now? It's just a dirty ol' river.
Is it? Heck, take one look at it! Ya must have a habit of livin' in real dirty places, Akiyama-san.
I can't really deny that.
That's not my point. It makes the city feel alive. Places that have pristine water are in the mountain wilderness, with no urban life to speak of.
Well, I s'pose so.
The river looks just the way it should for the greatest pleasure district in Kansai.
I want to dive into it. It seems poetically fitting, given that we're coming up on the end of the year, don't you think?
Eww, no! You might find that fun, but other folks would think you're an idiot. You could hit yer head and die, ya know.
Is it that terrible an idea?
This may just be me, but I'd find things more convenient without the river. Havin' to only cross at the bridges is kind of a big pain.
How can you say that? That's one of the big symbols of the city.
If ya want symbols, we've got plenty of big, gaudy, glowin' signs.
They do stand out. That strength of self-assertiveness is part of the Osaka vibe.
Yep! Nobody knows how to catch yer attention like the shops of Osaka!
I could learn from them. How about a cabaret club you can spot from one hundred meters away? That would be the talk of the town.
Good idea! And you could have a sign to show who the number one girl a' the month was, too! Like, check out this girl right here!
Oh, that's a great idea! I'm going to use that.
Just make sure ya pay me royalties!
Hah! You drive a hard bargain.
That isn't all. The signs are just flashy in order to get customers in, right? What's more important is the service you get when you're there.
Ya got it backwards. Of course the service is gonna be good, so ya gotta find other ways to distinguish yourself.
But there's always going to be a trade-off, depending on which you go with. If you focus on how things look outside, you'll neglect what's inside.
Hmph. You're a stubborn fella. I guess that's why the streets in Tokyo are so drab.
Diversity is what makes our country great after all.
It's like a theme park, like those ones with old Edo or German themes.
Oh, I like that! I'm a huge fan of theme parks. I wish we could make Sotenbori into one!
And you could shoot off flashy fireworks every night.
If we did that, I'd never be in the club. I'd go outside to watch the fireworks all the time!
Hey, now. We can't let the staff get distracted.
They aren't really that unusual.
Really? Ya think so?
I mean, they're very Osakan, sure. But they fit in with the city, so they don't really stand out that much.
If you want to talk weird and unusual, I think someplace like Akihabara is far more shocking.
I feel like ya wounded my hometown pride a little...
They're not just gaudy, they're strange. They're something unique, even in Japan.
I kinda like that! We're the only one and we're number one!
You can't really be number one if there's no one else competing...
All of this was normal for me growin' up, so it's hard for me to tell what shops there are when I'm goin' around Tokyo.
There are lots of places here where I can't tell that either.
There are a lot of strong-willed girls here in Osaka, aren't there?
What? That ain't true.
Sure it is.
Nah, you're talkin' about girls from soap operas and manga books. I don't like hearin' ya stereotype us as bein' headstrong.
Sorry. Did I offend you?
It's okay. We Osakan girls are big-hearted after all, so I can't be all that mad.
It's not just a stereotype. I've actually met girls who are like that.
I mean, I guess some girls are like that. But I wouldn't say that we're all that strong-willed.
It's not just some girls. I feel like all the girls I've met here have been like that.
Maybe that's just a coincidence. There are a lotta girls here in Osaka, y'know.
You're just in denial.
What's wrong with me tellin' ya you're wrong?
I bet the girls you're talkin' about are all older ladies, huh?
Yeah, the older women here sure seem tough.
Well, girls and older women ain't the same thing, so don't lump 'em together.
That's true. My mistake.
I'm glad ya finally understand!
Older ladies here in Osaka can be pretty darn scary. A younger gal like me could never hold her own against one of 'em.
Scary in what sense?
They wear this garish leopard print, and talk real loud. They can't stand bein' shown up and they never wanna admit they're wrong.
That is scary. Even I have to muster up the courage to strike up a conversation with them.
Aren't ya happier gettin' to talk to a cute and ladylike girl instead?
Should you be saying that about yourself?
Like you?
No, not like me! Were ya even listenin'? I'm not anythin' like an older woman!
No, I think you hit the nail right on the head.
I don't wear leopard print! Have ya seen what I normally wear?
What does wearing leopard print have to do with being strong-willed?
Hey, don't change the subject! We're talkin' about whether I'm an old lady or not!
